message.abstract: <jats:p>People are forming social interactions and expressing their thoughts in cyberspace as social networking services like Web 2.0 became more popular. Users of the internet have grown in popularity at a rapid rate, in tandem with new technologies who frequently voice their ideas on social media platforms, and personal blogs. They have both favourable and negative feelings regarding individuals, organisations, locations, and events. Natural language processing and machine learning techniques, as well as other approaches to working with vast amounts of text, allow for the extraction of attitudes from social platforms. In this paper, we present a novel knowledge-based strategy for detecting online communities that are producing social unrest. The goal of this research was to see if there was any useful information across social media platforms that may help with analysis of sentiments in specific contexts. This data is referred to as social context. The primary distinction between our research model and other community identification approaches is that, we want to find online user communities that are socially connected and have similar sentiments whereas others look for link structure based user communities. Faced with the threat of social unrest fuelled by social media, our proposed strategy can help the government organisations to ensure the tracking of information flow patterns across social media platforms and the influence of social network data that are fuelling ethnic tensions.</jats:p>
title: Fast Unfolding of Online Communities Causing Social Unrest Via Non Negative Matrix Factorization
